chapter: Louis Armstrong picture, Kid Rena record and Bunk
title: When the sock cymbal came in and the drumming on the Kid Rena record
summary: Rene dates the sock cymbal to about 1928-30. They note the record is mostly snare and bass, and Rene thinks he may have left the sock off.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: When did the sock cymbal come in? Yeah.
Oh, the sock cymbal come in here somewhere around, I believe, in 29, 30 or 28 or something like that. Like that. It went big, though.

Well, I noticed on the record there, the one that I'm giving you there, it's a, I don't know, maybe a little crash on the cymbal, you know, military style, you know. Yeah, I got a crash cymbal too. Yeah, but I mean, just one crash, you didn't play much sock cymbal on the record. Oh, baby. You don't have a phonograph here, do you?
We ain't hooked up, but we have one on the mic, you know. Oh, yeah. Yeah.

Well, you listen to that record, you'd be surprised because it's nearly all snare drumming, you know. All snare drumming. Yeah, well, I mean, that's what it was. Snare and bass, and that's it, you know. And then if they said a spot where a theme would end or something, you know, you might give a little rodling.
What song was that? Well, any of them. Oh, ain't them, yeah.
You know, I mean, but mostly snare and bass drumming on that record, I don't know why. But you used to play sock.
Well, maybe, maybe, maybe I might have left the sock off.
You might have left it at home or something.
I think, I think I might have left the sock off.
